_about: What each muscle does, from standard anatomy references (main actions only). Used by search so you can find muscles by movement. Keys are model names without .l/.r.
Levator scapulae: turns the neck to the same side
Transverse part of trapezius muscle: retracts the scapula (squeezes shoulder blades together)
Rhomboid major muscle: retracts the scapula (squeezes shoulder blades together)
Rhomboid minor muscle: retracts the scapula (squeezes shoulder blades together)
Serratus anterior muscle: holds the scapula against the ribs (prevents winging)
Pectoralis minor muscle: pulls the scapula forward and down
lifts the ribs when breathing hard
Sternocleidomastoid muscle: turns the head to the opposite side
lifts the breastbone when breathing hard
Scalenus anterior muscle: lifts the first rib when breathing
Scalenus medius muscle: lifts the first rib when breathing
Scalenus posterior muscle: lifts the second rib when breathing
Splenius capitis muscle: extends the head and neck (looking up)
turns the head to the same side
Splenius colli muscle: turns the neck to the same side
Semispinalis colli muscle: turns the neck to the opposite side
Rectus posterior major capitis muscle: turns the head to the same side
Obliquus inferior capitis muscle: turns the head to the same side
Platysma: tenses the skin of the neck
pulls the corners of the mouth down
Acromial part of deltoid muscle: raises the arm out to the side (abduction)
Supraspinatus muscle: starts raising the arm out to the side
holds the shoulder joint together (rotator cuff)
Infraspinatus muscle: holds the shoulder joint together (rotator cuff)
Teres minor muscle: holds the shoulder joint together (rotator cuff)
Subscapularis muscle: holds the shoulder joint together (rotator cuff)
Teres major muscle: pulls the arm down and back
Latissimus dorsi muscle: pulls the arm down and back (pull-ups, rowing)
Clavicular head of pectoralis major musc: brings the arm across the chest
Sternocostal head of pectoralis major mu: brings the arm across the chest
Coracobrachialis muscle: brings the arm toward the body
Flexor carpi radialis: tilts the wrist toward the thumb
Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris: tilts the wrist toward the little finger
Extensor carpi radialis longus: extends the wrist (back of hand up)
tilts the wrist toward the thumb
Extensor carpi radialis brevis: extends the wrist (back of hand up)
Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris: tilts the wrist toward the little finger
Flexor pollicis longus: bends the tip of the thumb
Abductor pollicis longus: moves the thumb away from the palm
Opponens pollicis muscle: brings the thumb across to touch the fingers (opposition)
Oblique head of adductor pollicis: pulls the thumb against the palm (pinch)
Lumbrical muscles of hand: bends the knuckles while straightening the fingers
Diaphragm: pulls the lungs down to fill them
External intercostal muscles: lift the ribs when breathing in
Internal intercostal muscles: pull the ribs down when breathing out hard
External abdominal oblique muscle: twists the trunk to the opposite side
Internal abdominal oblique muscle: twists the trunk to the same side
Quadratus lumborum muscle: steadies the twelfth rib when breathing
Multifidus lumborum muscle: extends and twists the lower back
Gluteus medius muscle: moves the leg out to the side
keeps the pelvis level when walking
Gluteus minimus muscle: moves the leg out to the side
keeps the pelvis level when walking
Tensor fasciae latae: moves the leg out to the side
Piriformis muscle: moves the bent thigh out to the side
Adductor longus: brings the thigh toward the other leg (adduction)
Adductor brevis: brings the thigh toward the other leg (adduction)
Adductor magnus: brings the thigh toward the other leg (adduction)
Gracilis muscle: brings the thigh toward the other leg
Pectineus muscle: brings the thigh toward the other leg
Sartorius muscle: lifts, opens and turns out the thigh (cross-legged sitting)
Abductor hallucis: moves the big toe away from the others
Medial pterygoid muscle: moves the jaw side to side
Inferior head of lateral pterygoid muscl: moves the jaw side to side
Zygomaticus major muscle: smiles (pulls the corner of the mouth up)
Mylohyoid muscle: raises the floor of the mouth (swallowing)
